summary: Round r1 (restricted network). Primary WTO documents on Nepal's use of special and differential treatment were located as leads: the 2025 Trade Policy Review (Secretariat report WT/TPR/S/478, Government report, chair's concluding remarks), Nepal's TFA categorisation in the TFA Database and notification portal, accession documents (WT/MIN(03)/19, WT/ACC/NPL/16) and goods schedule, WTO guidance on LDC graduation, the MC13 smooth-transition decision (via UN LDC Portal and MC13 documents) and MC14 LDC Group documents. No provision-level usage was retrieved; all items are pending. The key dependency is the UN graduation date (26C): LDC-specific S&DT lapses at graduation, so the pending UNGA decision on Nepal's extension request shifts the timing of every LDC-only provision.

findings.claim: Q1 TFA: Nepal's category A/B/C designations by measure, implementation dates notified and measures conditional on capacity-building support (category C).
findings.note: TFAD Nepal page B06 and notification portal B07; TPR S/478 B02 section on trade facilitation.

findings.claim: Q1 TRIPS: use of the LDC general transition period (Art. 66.1) and pharmaceutical transition; what ends at graduation.
findings.note: TPR S/478 B02 IP chapter; WTO graduation page B11; Council for TRIPS decisions (symbols to be taken from B11).

findings.claim: Q1 Accession-specific transition periods and commitments (WT/ACC/NPL/16) still running or expired.
findings.note: B08-B10: working party report commitment paragraphs with transition dates; goods schedule.

findings.claim: Q1 Agriculture/SPS/TBT/subsidies: notification compliance and use of LDC exemptions (e.g. export-subsidy and SCM Annex VII status, de minimis).
findings.note: S/478 notifications table B02; WTO documents online search required (not located).

findings.claim: Q1 Preferences received by Nepal as an LDC (DFQF schemes, LDC services waiver) and post-graduation treatment.
findings.note: B11, B16 and 16B leads; post-graduation timing depends on the UN graduation date (see 26C).

findings.claim: Q1 Post-graduation WTO smooth-transition entitlements (MC13 decision) and MC14 outcome on graduation-related S&DT.
findings.note: B12-B15; official MC13 decision symbol and MC14 outcome documents to be verified on docs.wto.org.

findings.claim: S&DT is classified into (i) LDC-specific provisions that lapse at graduation (subject to transition decisions), (ii) developing-member S&DT that Nepal retains after graduation, and (iii) accession-specific commitments; usage is evidenced only by notifications or WTO Secretariat documents, not by eligibility alone.

data_gaps: Full list of Nepal notifications by agreement (WTO Documents Online / notification portal export) not retrieved.
Council for TRIPS decision symbols on LDC transition periods not confirmed in r1.
MC14 outcome documents (adopted decisions) not located; only LDC Group declaration and draft package.
Utilisation of preferences (as opposed to eligibility) requires partner-country import data by preference regime (with 22-series agents).

assumptions.text: 'Uses' an S&DT provision means Nepal has notified, invoked or been recorded by the WTO Secretariat as applying it; eligibility alone is not counted as use.

challenges.text: EXP-13 should distinguish WTO LDC-specific S&DT (rules) from unilateral LDC preference schemes (market access); they lapse on different schedules after graduation.
Nepal Government TPR report hosted on giwmscdnone.gov.np (lead B03) and WTO documents mirrored on tralac have no catalog source id; confirm tier and add WTO Documents Online as endpoint.

uncertainty: High. No provision-level evidence retrieved. MC13 decision text is known only via a UN LDC Portal summary; MC14 outcome is unverified. Timing of loss of LDC-specific S&DT is conditional on the pending UNGA decision on Nepal's preparatory-period extension.
